title: Sequenced-span-hashes and tenant-affinity routing for on-prem observability
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Private/VPC collectors occasionally produce out-of-order spans when batching, buffering, or during intermittent egress to the control plane. This causes incorrect end-to-end latency calculation, skewed error attribution across tenants, and noisy dashboards for Dedicated and on-prem customers. Root causes observed in prior incidents: collector drain race conditions, cross-tenant multiplexing during backpressure, and ambiguous span timestamps when time-sync jitter occurs.
notes: This ticket implements a collector-side sequencing layer that stamps a compact sequenced-span-hash and an HMAC-backed sequence token at ingress. Combined with tenant-affinity routing and deterministic drain semantics, this enables stable span ordering and safe offline replay in air-gapped deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Collector ingress stamps every span/batch with a sequenced-span-hash and sequence_token (OTLP envelope extension) without altering original trace/span IDs
Per-tenant sequence_mode config (strict|relaxed) toggles reordering enforcement at drain time
Under simulated load (2k TPS, 500ms spike), observed out-of-order spans reduced to <0.5% for strict mode compared to current ~3% baseline
Dashboards expose new metrics: tenant.sequence_drop_rate, tenant.replay_offset_ms, tenant.sequence_hmac_failures
Offline replay tool can ingest signed sequences and reorder events deterministically in air-gapped clusters; playback validated against golden set in QA
Security: sequence_token signing uses customer KMS key or cluster-local HSM; design reviewed and approved by security team
Backward compatibility: collectors accept both legacy OTLP envelopes and the extended envelope; receivers gracefully ignore sequencing metadata when not supported
tasks: Design doc: explain sequenced-span-hash algorithm, HMAC layout, and mailbox buffer semantics (Confluence)
Collector change: add ingress stamping, per-tenant config, and deterministic drain pipeline
Router change: tenant-affinity sticky routing and per-tenant soft-quotas to avoid cross-tenant multiplexing under backpressure
Replay tool: implement offline replay utility that verifies HMACs and replays in sequence order
Metrics: add sequence-related telemetry and add rollout instrumentation for canary testing
Dashboards: create latency/error dashboards corrected for sequence reordering; add per-tenant replay/ordering visualizations
E2E tests: synthetic trace generator, golden ordering validator, and chaos tests for network partitions
Security review and KMS/HSM integration testing
Docs/Upgrade notes: collector config, runtime flags, and incompatibility warnings

implementation_notes: Key decisions: use a 64-bit rolling counter per-tenant plus a 16-bit bucket-derived salt to construct the sequenced-span-hash; HMAC with per-cluster KMS key; sequence_token contains cluster_id|tenant_id|counter|timestamp and is HMACed. Collector will expose a 'sequence_delay_ms' flag for drained windows to trade latency for ordering fidelity.
risks_mitigations: Risk: added metadata increases bandwidth and storage. Mitigation: compressed base64 encoding and opt-in per-tenant enablement; sampling for low-priority tenants.
Risk: HMAC key mismanagement. Mitigation: integrate with customer KMS, rotate keys, and fail-open policy that marks sequences as unsigned but ingests with lower trust level
Risk: replay could duplicate events. Mitigation: replay tool deduplicates using span_id + sequence_token and emits safe idempotency markers
